$comment: Hardware (device-lane) toolchain record. RETURN-4 P2-1 requires the
Maestro CLI to be pinned by VERSION and ARTIFACT CHECKSUM, because the
flow validator's per-command payload schemas are only meaningful
against a known CLI version, and because an unverified CLI download is
an unreviewed binary on the machine that sees the enrollment QR.
STATUS 2026-09-04: every MECHANICAL part of this record is filled and
verified on the Windows desktop. What remains is the ATTESTATION — a
person putting their name to it — which is why status is not yet
'pinned' and scripts/maestro-enroll-runner.mjs still refuses to run.
What was actually verified, so the attestation below is informed
rather than blind:
1. checksums_sha256.txt was fetched from the official cli-2.10.0
release and publishes 29b675e1...cd991 for maestro.zip.
2. maestro.zip (314,828,521 bytes) was downloaded from the official
release URL recorded below and its sha256 was COMPUTED locally:
it equals the published value. The digest here is that computed
value, not a number copied from a web page.
3. The release was extracted and compared against the CLI already
installed at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\maestro: 198 files in the
release, 198 in the install, none missing, and ZERO content
mismatches by sha256. The Maestro that runs the flows on this
machine is byte-identical to the official release artifact.
4. `maestro --version` reports 2.10.0, matching `version` below.
TO COMPLETE (Kody or the QA lead, and only this):
- satisfy yourself that the four points above are the verification
you want standing behind the device lane;
- set verifiedBy to your name and verifiedOn to the date;
- set status to 'pinned'.
The runner then stops refusing, and mfa-enroll.yaml, mfa-login.yaml and
confinement-probe.yaml become runnable. Re-run maestro:validate after
filling this record: the payload schemas are declared to match this
exact version.
Note on what a checksum can and cannot say: points 1-3 establish that
the installed binary is the artifact the vendor published. They do not
review what that artifact does. That is the judgement the signature is
for.

maestro.installCommand: extract maestro.zip so that maestro/bin and maestro/lib land in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\maestro, then add %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\maestro\bin to PATH (this is the layout verified byte-for-byte on the desktop)
maestro.installedTreeVerification: 198/198 files sha256-identical to the extracted official release; 0 missing, 0 mismatched
maestro.schemaBasis: scripts/maestro-validate.mjs per-command payload schemas are declared against the pinned version recorded here

deviceLane.reason: Android half executing on the desktop's Pixel_8 API 35 AVD against the live CLI stack; 11 of 17 flows pass as of 2026-09-04. The iOS half stays HOLD on hardware nobody has (see docs/plans). Three of the six held flows are held by this record's missing attestation.
